critical_code_review_comments: Fix is CSS-only, minimal and well-scoped. Comments in CSS clearly reference BUG-2026-10-12-006. .cdl-wrap{width:100%} + .cdl-strip{min-width:0;max-width:100%;overflow-x:auto} is the correct idiomatic fix for a horizontally scrolling child inside a flex parent with align-items:center (which otherwise sizes to intrinsic content width).

rca of the issue: Parent row (.price-row-input in ReviewOrder.jsx L2079) uses column flex with inherited align-items:center. Before fix, .cdl-strip had no width constraint, so overflow-x:auto could not contain content; the flex child grew to its intrinsic (scrollWidth=1113px) size, overflowing the 390px viewport. Adding width:100% on .cdl-wrap and min-width:0;max-width:100% on .cdl-strip forces the scroller to clamp to its parent and clip overflow internally. Verified: html.scrollWidth==clientWidth==390, strip.scrollWidth=1113 but strip.clientWidth=324 (contained), strip.scrollLeft advances independently of document.scrollLeft.
